To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) woodland birds were well represented across a range of agricultural landscapes; (2) woodland birds were more common in landscapes with more wooded habitat; and (3) woodland birds used scattered trees and tree plantations to enhance their population status beyond that provided by native vegetation cover.

(1) woodland birds are well represented in agricultural landscapes; and (2) woodland birds are positively associated with woodland vegetation cover in the landscape, and that the incidence of 12 woodland bird species is positively related to the cover of scattered trees and/or plantations in agricultural landscapes.
woodland bird communities in agricultural mosaicks were well represented, but many species were restricted to landscapes with a substantial area of remnant native vegetation cover.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conservation of woodland birds at the landscape scale in agricultural mosaic environments.
the value of woodland habitat at the landscape level in agricultural environments.
the conservation of woodland birds in agricultural environments, and the value of ‘countryside vegetation’ at the landscape scale.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the conservation of native vegetation is critical for biodiversity in agricultural environments, but supplementary management of other wooded elements in the matrix may be necessary to ensure that woodland-dependent species persist.
the conservation of woodland birds in agricultural environments is enhanced by the presence of a range of woodland habitats at the landscape scale.
the conservation value of wooded countryside elements in agricultural environments is highly variable among species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
woodland bird species are not limited by the amount of native vegetation cover in farmland landscapes, and are not restricted to woodland habitat.
woodland bird species in agricultural environments are sustained by a combination of woodland cover in native vegetation, scattered trees and tree plantations.

woodland birds are well-represented in agricultural mosaicks and that the incidence of 23 woodland species was positively related (and in some cases, significantly related) to measures of wooded vegetation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conservation of woodland birds in agricultural landscapes can be improved by the careful management of tree plantations, scattered trees and native vegetation cover.
woodland-dependent birds are well represented in farmland mosaicks, and the incidence of many species is enhanced by wooded cover.
the conservation of woodland birds is best achieved through a landscape-scale approach that includes native vegetation, but also the careful management of scattered trees and tree plantations.
